timeline.event: Mumtaz Mahal dies; Shah Jahan commissions the Taj Mahal
Construction begins under architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori
Main mausoleum structure completed
Entire complex completed — gardens, mosque, guest house
UNESCO World Heritage Site designation
Construction begins when Shah Jahan shifts capital to Delhi
Fort completed; becomes the residence of Mughal emperors
Nadir Shah invades and loots the fort including the Peacock Throne
Last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar holds court here during the revolt
UNESCO World Heritage Site designation

name: Qutub Minar
builder: Qutb ud-Din Aibak, continued by Iltutmish

timeline.event: Construction begun by Qutb ud-Din Aibak after defeating the last Hindu kingdom in Delhi
Top three storeys completed by Iltutmish
Top storey damaged by lightning; Firoz Shah Tughlaq repairs and adds two more storeys
UNESCO World Heritage Site designation
Construction begins under Emperor Vespasian
Inaugurated by Emperor Titus with 100 days of games
Major fire caused by lightning damages the upper levels
Powerful earthquake causes the entire south side to collapse
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site

name: Eiffel Tower
unesco_status: Part of 'Paris, Banks of the Seine' UNESCO site (1991)

timeline.event: Maurice Koechlin and Émile Nouguier create the initial design
Construction begins on the Champ de Mars
Completed for the Exposition Universelle; becomes world's tallest structure at 300m
Antenna added, increasing height to 330m
Included in the UNESCO 'Paris, Banks of the Seine' World Heritage Site
Great Pyramid of Khufu construction begins
Great Pyramid completed — tallest man-made structure for 3,800 years
Pyramid of Khafre and the Great Sphinx constructed
Pyramid of Menkaure, the smallest of the three, completed
Memphis Necropolis designated UNESCO World Heritage Site

name: Machu Picchu
builder: Emperor Pachacuti of the Inca Empire

timeline.event: Built as an estate for Emperor Pachacuti
Abandoned during the Spanish Conquest
Rediscovered by American historian Hiram Bingham III
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh so royal women could observe street life without being seen
Jaipur painted pink to welcome Prince of Wales — Hawa Mahal included
Major restoration project completed
Construction begins under King Suryavarman II
Temple complex completed — largest religious monument in the world
Gradually converted from Hindu to Buddhist temple
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Foundation stone laid to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary
Construction completed; ceremonial arch opened
Last British troops march through the Gateway, symbolizing the end of British rule in India
Construction begins under Pericles' building program
Colossal chryselephantine statue of Athena by Phidias installed
Sculptural decoration completed
Venetian bombardment causes massive explosion, destroying the roof
Acropolis designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site

name: Statue of Liberty
builder: Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi (sculptor), Alexandre Gustave Eiffel (structural engineer)

timeline.event: Construction begins in France
Statue completed in Paris and disassembled for shipping
Dedicated in New York Harbor — a gift from France
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
